exposure: Two stitches for emergency cervical cerclage
One stitch for emergency cervical cerclage
outcome: Neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admissions rate
cohort: The study included 26 women with singleton pregnancies who underwent emergency cervical cerclage before 26 weeks.
finding: Emergency cervical cerclage using two stitches significantly prolonged pregnancy and improved neonatal prognosis (reduced NICU admissions and length of stay) compared to the one-stitch procedure.
gest_age: Participants underwent cerclage before 26 weeks; average gestational age at delivery was 32.71 ± 5.54 weeks for the two-stitches group and 27.99 ± 4.70 weeks for the one-stitch group.
